_fixture_note: MG-23 destroy circuit-breaker fixture — the AUTHORIZED destroy. Two destructive changes (`delete:module.native_otlp.azurerm_container_app.collector` and `delete:module.native_otlp.azapi_resource.otlp_dcr`) amongst benign ones: a deliberate teardown of two retired resources, reviewed by the operator, who then re-runs the branch-restricted workflow_dispatch RECOVERY path with TF_DESTROY_GUARD_AUTHORIZED_CHANGES naming exactly those two tokens. THE OVERRIDE IS AN EXACT SET OF ACTION-QUALIFIED CHANGE TOKENS (`<action>:<address>[#deposed=<key>]`) — NOT a count and NOT a bare address. The count form TF_DESTROY_GUARD_EXPECTED_DESTROYS and the action-unqualified form TF_DESTROY_GUARD_AUTHORIZED_DESTROYS are BOTH RETIRED, and the gate now fails loudly if either is set rather than ignoring it. A count was retired because it authorizes an ARITY: this document is paired with destroy-guard-override-setdiff.json, which has the SAME two-destroy arity over the Cosmos account and the IoT Hub, so a count of 2 issued for two disposable collector resources would equally have cleared total data loss. The runner exercises this ONE document many ways: no override must FAIL (an unattended apply never destroys); the exact two tokens must PASS; the same tokens REORDERED and duplicated must PASS (the comparison is set equality, not string equality); the OTHER document's arity-matching token set must FAIL; a SUBSET must FAIL (an unapproved destroy remains); a SUPERSET must FAIL (this is not the plan that was reviewed); the same addresses qualified `forget:` instead of `delete:` must FAIL (orphaning a live resource out of Terraform management and destroying it are different decisions); the bare unqualified addresses must FAIL; and `2`, `all`, `true`, `-1` and `*` must all FAIL — there is no numeric, boolean or wildcard escape hatch.
